summary: Botswana’s restoration commitments aim to rehabilitate 10% of degraded land and plant 1,200,000 trees, while a mixed restoration-conservation pledge sets bush encroachment control at 50%. Conservation targets include retaining 163,370 km2 of core wildlife refugia, equivalent to about 28.1% of the country’s total land area; providing two artificial water points per protected area; preventing alien invasive species spread by 10%; managing 25% through veldt-fire management; and applying an ecosystems-based approach for 80% in relation to extreme events such as floods and storms. Relative to the 2022 land-cover map, the refuge target is numerically equivalent to about 35.8% of current shrubland, although its land-cover composition is not specified.

targets.context: ≈28.1% of total land area; numerically equivalent to ≈35.8% of current shrubland area

targets.unit: number of boreholes per protected area
